questions.q: What is the main drawback of the coaxial X8 layout?
questions.explain: The bottom prop works in the wash of the top one. You pay for compactness and fault tolerance with efficiency.

questions.q: What do you fix first when VIBE is high on large props?
options: The PID gains and D-term filters on the yaw axis
questions.explain: Prop and motor balancing, frame stiffness, FC damping. Filters are the last resort.

questions.q: When do you test a motor failure?
options: SITL, then at altitude with no payload
Right away with a full payload, to test the worst case
On the bench with the props on
questions.explain: Fault tolerance is tested, not assumed.

"Hover throttle" in ArduPilot terms is the hover thrust as a fraction of maximum (≈ 1/(T/W)), not the percent throttle on a thrust stand; it is refined in flight (MOT_HOVER_LEARN), and altitude hold depends on it.

options: The maximum roll angle in centidegrees
questions.explain: The motor output (PWM) reserved for yaw at saturation; yaw is the lowest-priority attitude axis: roll and pitch come first, yaw keeps at least this headroom, and throttle gets what is left.

questions.q: How do you safely test a motor failure on an X8?
options: Take a prop off in flight
The applet in SITL, then with no payload
Disconnect an ESC on the ground with the props on
It cannot be tested at all
questions.explain: motor_failure_test first in SITL, then at altitude with no payload; MOT_STOP_BITMASK plus a switch.

questions.q: Why is a heavy vehicle tuned more slowly and carefully than a 5"?
options: High inertia and slow motors: mistakes take longer to build up and are more dangerous
ArduPilot does not support large props
questions.explain: Large props and mass mean slow dynamics and a high cost of error.
